---
title: "Caveat and Limitation"
author: "Yun Jiang"
---

## caveat

1. M: Cron `c9bc25a4` fires at 17:59, not 18:00 — the scheduler's fixed
   early offset for one-shots pinned to :00.
2. M: If Claude Code is closed at 17:59, the durable one-shot does not
   run then; it surfaces for catch-up at the next launch.
3. M: cs-derived metrics count a supplementary/secondary record only when
   that record carries the `cs` tag — an aligner-dependent input property,
   not guaranteed by the format.
4. L: QC-fail (0x200) and duplicate (0x400) records are also included in
   every metric; no filter for them exists in the codebase.
5. M: "Never decided" in the record-universe audits means no recorded
   decision — the attribution rests on absent filters and commit
   messages; unrecorded deliberation cannot be ruled out.
6. M: the 2026-11-18 secondary-exclusion agreement is design-level; the
   numeric impact on existing datasets was not measured (no BAM scanned
   this turn, and per user instruction pipeline data was not consulted).
7. M: 0.9.0 outputs shrink wherever secondary records exist — do not mix
   0.8.x and 0.9.x outputs in cross-version comparisons.
8. L: annotate output BAMs from 0.9.0 carry no tags on secondary records
   (0.8.x tagged them) — downstream tag filters see a behavioral change.
9. H: an env that lists `sam-tagger` without a version pin moves to 0.9.0
   from sibio on its next solve — read counts and depth then drop on BAMs
   with secondary alignments; pin `sam-tagger=0.8.*` where 0.8.x output is
   required.
10. M: rolling items 1-2 still name 0.8.x as the ecsngsqc and wps_1012
    migration target — left unchanged on 2026-11-23; decide whether they
    move to 0.9.x.
11. M: the v0.9.0 recipe and audit commits in conda-recipes are local only
    — the remote conda-recipes repo does not carry the 0.9.0 recipe.
12. H: the per-base Python loop as the cause of the pileup slowness is a
    hypothesis from arithmetic (about 0.53 µs per counted base) and code
    reading; cron `409a7590` must measure it.
13. M: cron `409a7590` profiles the head (0.9.0), which skips secondary
    records; the 2026-11-18 runs used 0.8.0 per the env pin, so timings
    and outputs can differ from the originals.
14. M: the cron fires at 18:01 only while a Claude Code session in this
    repo is open and idle; otherwise the durable one-shot surfaces for
    catch-up at the next launch.
15. L: the machine carried a load average of 8.3 on 12 cores at 16:27;
    other jobs running at 18:01 can inflate the measured times.

## limitation

1. M: This turn scheduled the analysis only; it did not itself examine
   whether error-stats metrics include supplementary records.
2. M: The 2026-11-16 record-universe audit is static code reading plus
   existing test assertions; no new BAM fixture was run this turn.
3. L: The downstream ecsngsqc workflow's interpretation of these columns
   was not audited.
4. L: The provenance trace stops at this repo's scaffold (c0a80c4);
   cs-tagger, the pre-port ancestor, has no history here.
5. M: The 2026-11-23 release covers the GitHub release and the sibio
   channel only — not bioconda and not PyPI.
6. M: The fresh-env check covered `--version` and import on this machine;
   other clients and other pixi versions were not tested.
7. M: This turn read rule logs, BAM indexes, output Parquet metadata and
   code; it did not run or profile `sam-tagger pileup`.
8. L: This turn did not count secondary records in the two BAMs and did
   not inspect the solved env of the 2026-11-18 run.
9. L: This turn did not test whether py-spy installs and traces on this
   machine.
